profile.reading: Lumos Networks is a fiber-based telecommunications provider whose roots trace to NTELOS Holdings, a Mid-Atlantic carrier headquartered in Waynesboro, Virginia; Lumos was spun off from NTELOS in 2011 and, per its own regulatory filings, operated an extensive Mid-Atlantic fiber footprint spanning roughly 9,200 route miles across 24 markets in Virginia, Pennsylvania, West Virginia, Maryland, Ohio, and Kentucky, serving carrier, enterprise, and data-center customers. Rather than a single flagship data center, that footprint included dozens of network facilities of varying size -- filings describe 36 data centers along its network, of which seven were company-owned colocation sites, with the rest likely representing smaller equipment huts, central-office collocation space, and points of presence supporting fiber-to-cell and enterprise connections. EQT Infrastructure acquired Lumos Networks in a deal valued at roughly $950 million, completing the sale in November 2017 and taking the fiber network private. In the years since, the Lumos brand has also become associated with a separate, EQT-backed residential fiber-to-the-home venture that has been actively building out gigabit fiber service in Virginia and North Carolina, including a publicly announced investment of more than $20 million to bring fiber internet to roughly 18,000 homes and businesses in the Lynchburg, Virginia region (Bedford and Campbell counties) -- though that announcement describes a service buildout across a multi-county area rather than a single facility. This registry entry is tied to a mapped point in Lynchburg, but the coordinates resolve, via standard geocoding, to a downtown building otherwise associated with BWXT, a nuclear-technology manufacturer unrelated to Lumos; the two companies may share a downtown Lynchburg building housing telecom equipment closets alongside BWXT's own operations, or the mapped location may be imprecise. No Lumos-specific street address, building type, square footage, or power figure for a Lynchburg facility is published by the company, and no Lynchburg city permit or assessor record confirming a Lumos-owned building at this location has been identified. What can be said with confidence is that Lumos operates network and small-format colocation infrastructure throughout its Mid-Atlantic territory, that Lynchburg sits within its historical NTELOS/Lumos service area, and that the company has recently been investing in expanding fiber connectivity to the Lynchburg region -- but the specific building represented by this map point cannot be confirmed from public sources.
